title: Butter-Washed Bourbon: Grated Butter Infusion and Two Flavor Outputs
summary: The video demonstrates a butter-based fat-wash technique inspired by bacon-wash, using grated butter to infuse bourbon and extract two products: bourbon-flavored butter and butter-flavored bourbon. The presenter grates two sticks of butter, packs them into a mason jar, pours bourbon (7 oz used in the example), and refrigerates the mixture for 1–2 days before straining through cheesecloth. The resulting infused liquids are then used in cocktails (notably Manhattan and Old Fashioned) and in a fall-inspired recipe (Autumn in New England) featuring sage, maple syrup, apple cider, and cider vinegar. The clip also suggests uses for the butter (hot honey as a compound butter, buttercream for cupcakes, or spreading on toast) and notes storage timelines for both the butter and the spirit, with a nod to Cook’s Illustrated as the source of the technique. The content addresses optional spirit substitutions (rye, rum, tequila) and invites viewer engagement in the comments.
topics: storage: butter a few days; spirits ~ two weeks
